title: Canonical pullback on affine Picard n-torsion is bijective
statement: Let $k\subseteq k\prime$ be algebraically closed fields [def-sc-field-extension], let $f:C\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ be a smooth connected affine curve [def-sc-curves], and let $P$ with projections $\pi:P\to C$ and $g:P\to\operatorname{Spec}k\prime$ be a pullback square for this extension. For $n\geq1$ nonzero in $k$, the canonical map $\{L\in\operatorname{Pic}(C):L^n=1\}\to\{M\in\operatorname{Pic}(P):M^n=1\}$ sending $L$ to $\pi^*L$ [def-sc-picard-group] is bijective.

source.place: Proper-case Kummer naturality sentence and affine-case Picard-torsion paragraph

proof.text: By [lem-sc-compactification], choose a smooth proper connected compactification. By [thm-sc-jacobian-representability], choose its Jacobian. By [lem-sc-pic-affine-quotient], the boundary is nonempty; choose a boundary point, which is rational because k is algebraically closed. Apply the affine Picard base-change compatibility theorem to obtain presentations Pic(C)=G/Lambda and Pic(P)=Gprime/Lambdaprime, compatible with pullback and identifying the two boundary subgroups. Identify the degree-zero Picard groups G and Gprime with points of the Jacobians.

Use the algebraically closed abelian-variety estimate, clauses (c) and (d): n multiplication on G is surjective and the map on G[n] is bijective. Injectivity on points is elementary: a k-point is determined by its image point and its residue-field map to k; equality after extension recovers both, since k to kprime is injective. These properties are transported through the Jacobian identification.

Injectivity: a representative mapping into Lambdaprime is the image of some lambda in Lambda; injectivity on points makes the representatives equal. Surjectivity: for y with ny in Lambdaprime, lift ny to lambda in Lambda and divide lambda by n in G to obtain x. Then y-j(x) is n-torsion. Lift this difference through G[n] to t; the class of x+t is n-torsion and maps to the class of y. This is the representative form of the divisible-quotient-torsion exact sequence. Compatibility of the presentations identifies the resulting bijection with the stated subtype map.

Transport from the categorical pullback to the specified pullback square using its canonical isomorphism. Picard pullback along an isomorphism is a group isomorphism and preserves torsion. The formula for the subtype map holds by construction. For n=1 its source and target are singleton types; n=0 is excluded.

lean.statement:
theorem affine_picard_torsion_base_change
    (k k' : Type u) [Field k] [Field k'] [IsAlgClosed k] [IsAlgClosed k'] [Algebra k k']
    (C : Scheme.{u}) (f : C ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsConnectedCurve f] [Smooth f] [IsAffine C]
    (P : Scheme.{u}) (π : P ⟶ C) (g : P ⟶ Spec (.of k'))
    (hπ : IsPullback π g f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k k'))))
    (n : ℕ) [NeZero n] (hn : (n : k) ≠ 0) :
    Function.Bijective (fun x : {x : C.Pic // x ^ n = 1} =>
      (⟨Scheme.Pic.map π x.1, by
        change (Scheme.Pic.mapHom π x.1) ^ n = 1
        rw [← map_pow, x.2, map_one]⟩ : {x : P.Pic // x ^ n = 1}))
